name: Acyclovir
summary: A guanosine analog antiviral used mainly for HSV and VZV, where early treatment makes the largest difference.
good: HSV/VZV treatment or prophylaxis when appropriate.
bad: Ignoring kidney function in higher-risk patients.
clinicalPearls: Starting early is more important than trying to rescue a late lesion with a perfect dose.
mechanism: After viral thymidine kinase activation, it inhibits viral DNA polymerase and terminates chain elongation.
indications: Herpes simplex, shingles, and prophylaxis or treatment in selected immunocompromised settings.
interactionNotes: Other nephrotoxic exposures can compound renal risk.

warnings: Renal dose adjustment and hydration matter, especially with IV use.
